data.narrative:
Resolute Grid is a seed-stage company operating in the Climate & Energy sector. The valuation universe comprises 9 sector peers: 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer set lacks sufficient density at the seed stage or adjacent stages with comparable valuations to support a reliable peer-median multiple approach.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. A search across same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier filters yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category, falling short of the minimum threshold needed for statistical confidence. While 9 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters produced zero matches in each critical dimension, indicating substantial dispersion in stage, scale, and valuation within the Climate & Energy universe. Attempting an all-sector median would introduce material noise and misalign stage and business model characteristics.

Given the inapplicability of peer comparables, alternative methods such as discounted cash flow analysis, market-sizing approaches, or early-stage venture benchmarking would be necessary to establish a defensible valuation range. The key uncertainties center on the lack of direct comparable transactions at seed stage and the heterogeneity of business models within climate tech—from hardware to materials to energy systems. Additional diligence on company-specific milestones and capital efficiency would be required to anchor a valuation.
